title: Security & Privacy Review - Northern Clinic
topics: model training policy (no training on customer data)
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked through SOC2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO options, audit log granularity and retention, KMS integration for key management, and explicit confirmation that customer prompts/data are not used to train public models. Customer requested SOC2 report, encryption KMS diagram, and a pilot checklist for PHI handling.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary (by 2026-06-20)
Diego to share KMS/HSM integration diagram and recommended architecture (by 2026-06-22)
Schedule a short pilot on dedicated tenant with EU region data residency (proposed 2026-06-29)
Provide written confirmation on training policy and data retention windows (by 2026-06-20)
action_items: Maya Chen | Send SOC2 Type II PDF + ISO/PCI matrix | 2026-06-20
Diego Alvarez | Share KMS integration architecture & sample terraform snippets | 2026-06-22
Priya Mehta | Provide sample data classification and pilot acceptance criteria | 2026-06-24
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we should be on the hour, i'm maya from redwood inference, and with me is diego our solutions engineer.  Sara? Tom? you there?
[00:08] Sara Patel: yeah hi thanks, we got a pretty packed agenda around security and data handling, appreciate you making time.
[00:16] Diego Alvarez: great, quick intro from our side then we'll jump into docs and questions. i know you sent a list in the email so we'll try to follow that.
[00:28] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. our main asks: can you confirm SOC 2 and ISO posture, how RBAC and SSO work with our okta setup, details on audit logs (what's captured, retention), encryption and KMS options, and then importantly — how you handle prompts/outputs and whether anything is used to train models. we also have PHI concerns.
[00:47] Maya Chen: totally, and we're prepared to walk through each. quick high level: redwood offers hosted and private deployment options, dedicated capacity with tenant isolation, and we support bring-your-own-KMS integrations for key control. SOC 2 Type II in our docs, ISO artifacts we can share under NDA.
[01:05] Sara Patel: ok good. for SOC 2, are there any gap items specific to healthcare? our compliance team will want to review controls mapping.
[01:14] Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll include a controls mapping to HIPAA-relevant controls in the SOC 2 report we send. note: while SOC 2 isn't the same as a HIPAA attestation, the mapping helps you see coverage for things like access control, encryption, and monitoring.
[01:29] Priya Mehta: can you describe RBAC? we need role separation and fine-grained permissions — e.g., devs vs ops vs compliance.
[01:37] Maya Chen: our platform uses role-based access controls with predefined roles and custom roles. you can restrict access at org, project, and route levels. SSO works via SAML with Okta and can enforce SCIM provisioning if you want automated user lifecycle. we'll share the RBAC matrix.
[01:54] Alex Gordon: and audit logs? we need immutable logs for admin actions, model access, and data access events. retention needs to be at least 1 year, potentially longer.
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: audit logs capture admin config changes, user sign-ins, API calls (including request metadata), model deployments, and token-level cost attribution. logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder or to cloud storage. retention is configurable; hosted default is 90 days, but for enterprise we offer extended retention as an add-on — we'll include options.
[02:27] Tom Reynolds: default 90 days isn't going to cut it. what about pushing to our S3 in eu-west and controlling retention ourselves?
[02:34] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can stream audit logs to customer-owned S3 in eu-west under dedicated/private; for hosted we also support log forwarding to your splunk/etl. for full isolation we recommend dedicated tenant + private deployment.
[02:46] Sara Patel: data residency, can we ensure prompts and embeddings never leave eu?
[02:51] Maya Chen: with dedicated eu region and private, yes we can pin data to a region. hosted tenants can be provisioned in eu-west. note that any external integrations (e.g., downstream analytics) need to be region-aware.
[03:03] Priya Mehta: encryption — we want BYOK and HSM-backed keys. how does KMS integration work?
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and external HSMs for private deployments. key usage is logged; keys never leave your control. we'll send a KMS integration diagram and sample policy snippets.
[03:22] Maya Chen: also DB-at-rest and in-transit encryption are on by default. TLS for all traffic.
[03:27] Tom Reynolds: good. now the big one — prompt retention and training. we need explicit confirmation: you do not use our prompts or outputs to further train or improve your public models, correct?
[03:39] Maya Chen: correct. we have a clear policy: customer data is not used to train or fine-tune our models unless a customer explicitly opts into that program. for hosted API customers on standard tier, we do not use customer content for model training. for customers that opt into shared-feedback or opt-in programs we ask for explicit consent.
[03:57] Sara Patel: can you put that in writing? our legal wants a statement and where it's documented.
[04:02] Maya Chen: yes, we'll provide a written training policy and a short attestation you can include in your vendor risk assessment.
[04:10] Alex Gordon: you mentioned caching earlier — do you cache prompts or KV cache that might reveal PII?
[04:16] Diego Alvarez: we do support prefix/KV caching for performance, but in dedicated/private deployments caching stays in the tenant. for hosted customers, caching is ephemeral and bounded; we can disable caching for sensitive workloads. caching configuration is per-route.
[04:30] Priya Mehta: PHI — if we have PHI in prompts, what are recommended steps? redwood needs to handle logs, retention, and ensure redaction.
[04:39] Diego Alvarez: recommended: use dedicated tenant, enable encryption with your KMS, disable request-logging of raw prompts to long term store, and apply redaction middleware on the client side (we can provide libraries). for our managed logging, you can choose to redact or not store prompt content.
[04:56] Tom Reynolds: ok, do you have a data retention policy for prompts? like 30 days, 90 days?
[05:01] Maya Chen: default hosted retention is 90 days for request traces and 30 days for raw prompt content, but these are configurable for enterprise. we can provide 0 retention (no persistent storage of raw content) if you need. we'll include the exact retention SLA in the docs.
[05:16] Sara Patel: we'd like an option for 'no retention' of raw prompts unless explicitly opted in.
[05:21] Maya Chen: that's supported for enterprise/dedicated.
[05:25] Priya Mehta: liability and breach notification timelines?
[05:29] Diego Alvarez: our incident response playbook includes 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, and we can integrate with your IR processes. we'll share the runbook excerpt.
[05:39] Tom Reynolds: about SAML/SSO — can you enforce device or IP restrictions?
[05:44] Maya Chen: we integrate with Okta and honor conditional access policies; you can enforce MFA and device posture via Okta rules.
[05:52] Alex Gordon: audit log format — do you provide immutable hashes or just events? we need tamper evidence.
[05:58] Diego Alvarez: we provide signed log delivery options and can store logs in a write-once bucket or forward to your SIEM; we also support pushing logs through an append-only stream with signatures for extra assurance.
[06:11] Sara Patel: excellent. one more on model variants — if there's fallback to cheaper models, is that logged and auditable?
[06:18] Maya Chen: yes, routing decisions and fallback events are recorded in the request metadata so you can see per-request model variant used, latency and token counts.
[06:26] Tom Reynolds: ok thank you.
[06:28] Maya Chen: quick demo of the security console? i can share a screen to show RBAC and logs — do you want that now or save it for the follow-up?
[06:36] Priya Mehta: quick peek would be useful, 10 minutes.
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: i'll share the log view; bear with me while i pull it up.
[06:52] [screen share noise] Diego Alvarez: so here is the audit stream, you can filter by user, action, resource, and time window. each event includes a request id, model variant, and tenant id.
[07:08] Sara Patel: looks good. can we see a sample of the SOC2 report redacted?
[07:13] Maya Chen: yes, i'll attach the redacted PDF after the call.
[07:17] Tom Reynolds: service availability and SLA question — do you offer uptime SLA and a runbook?
[07:22] Maya Chen: for dedicated customers we offer SLA-backed uptime with credits. runbooks and playbooks are provided for private deployments.
[07:29] Alex Gordon: any third-party subprocessors? we need a list for our vendor assessment.
[07:34] Diego Alvarez: yes we'll provide the subprocessors list; typical ones include cloud infra providers and monitoring vendors. we'll supply the most up-to-date roster.
[07:41] Priya Mehta: regarding data deletion — if we terminate, what's the deletion timeline?
[07:46] Maya Chen: standard deletion window is 30 days post-termination for hosted, but for enterprise we support immediate deletion and certifiable erasure. we'll include the certificate process.
[07:57] Tom Reynolds: ok great. a couple of clarifying questions from compliance doc: do you ever perform ad-hoc manual access to customer data for debugging?
[08:05] Diego Alvarez: by policy, engineers do not have blanket access. access for debugging requires an escalation process with approvals, is logged in audit trails, and we can offer a session recording. manual access is rare and governed by policy.
[08:18] Sara Patel: please include that escalation workflow in the docs.
[08:22] Maya Chen: will do.
[08:25] Tom Reynolds: last question — encryption in transit to the model runtime, are ephemeral keys used for intra-cluster?
[08:31] Diego Alvarez: yes, intra-cluster traffic is encrypted and uses ephemeral session keys; for private deployments you can opt for mTLS with your own CA.
[08:40] Priya Mehta: great. any caveats about dev environments and telemetry? we don't want dev logs mixing with prod.
[08:46] Diego Alvarez: dev vs prod separated by project/tenant; telemetry is segmented and can be routed to different destinations. we'll share best-practices for environment separation.
[08:58] Maya Chen: recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2+ISO artifacts, KMS diagram, written training-policy attestation, RBAC matrix, and propose pilot dates.
[09:09] Tom Reynolds: sounds good. thanks.
[09:12] Sara Patel: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:14] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar for the pilot.
[09:20] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings present (e.g., some technical terms might appear slightly off), speaker labels accurate for majority of the call.
